pages.text: Mrs. Magpie, who saw everything from the roof, came to the shop holding a basket. Inside, a baby magpie chirped. Coco the little mouse hopped. "A baby magpie! I want to hold the baby too!"
She offered the basket. "Could you hold the baby for a moment?" Coco lifted the baby high with both paws and hugged tight! Little wings fluttered. Cheep!
Coco pushed a whole crescent loaf toward the baby's beak. "Eat, eat!" The beak was as small as a bean. The bread wouldn't fit. The baby turned away and cried, cheep, cheep!

Mrs. Magpie first wrapped the baby gently in her wing to soothe it. "Coco, a baby is very small. Hold gently." Coco brought their empty paws together in front of their tummy. "Did I hurt the baby...?"
She tore off a bean-sized bit of bread and offered it at the baby's beak. The baby took it. Yum. She whispered, "A crumb as small as the beak. Baby magpie—gently!"
Coco opened both paws wide and gently received the baby, as if touching feathers or holding a cloud. The baby stayed still without fluttering.
Coco tore off a bean-sized bit and gently placed it before the beak. Yum, yum, and yum again. Coco tightened the scarf knot with both paws. "Baby magpie—gently!"
The baby drifted to sleep on Coco's front paws. Coco breathed softly and moved their tail gently. Mrs. Magpie nodded beside them.

When the baby woke and opened its beak, Coco offered another bean-sized piece. "One, hold gently! Two, a crumb as small as the beak! Three, quiet when the baby sleeps!" Coco's paws didn't hurry at all.

Mrs. Magpie wrapped Coco warmly in her wing. "You took good care of the baby!" Even paws that press dough hard can send a baby to sleep when used gently. Coco looked at the baby and whispered, "Baby magpie—gently!"
